cross_case_findings: All 24 cases were read independently. Rates use sector_delta * 512 / 1048576 / window_s; write ratio uses logical_write_bytes / (write_sector_delta * 512); full pressure percentages use delta_us / (window_s * 1000000) * 100; completion_ratio is completion_ms / baseline_completion_ms, so values above 1 mean slower completion. All requested metrics are rounded to six decimals.

C1W1S1, C1W1S7, C1W1S13 and C1W1S19 show long readers, 8000-page WAL growth, zero checkpoint progress and 12.500000% to 20.000000% I/O full pressure. Each also has one copy operation. Reader-pinned checkpoints are strongly supported; copy versus SQLite attribution of I/O pressure is unresolved, and completion is only 1.025000 times baseline.

C1W1S2, C1W1S8, C1W1S14 and C1W1S20 show 300 MiB available, bidirectional swapping and 7.058824% to 10.909091% memory full pressure. Their 2.250000 completion ratio and slow sends point toward local memory pressure despite very low I/O full pressure; low I/O pressure does not exclude reclaim stalls.

C1W1S3, C1W1S9, C1W1S15 and C1W1S21 show provider 429 responses and a 2.125000 completion ratio with short sends, negligible local pressure and progressing checkpoints. Provider delay is more strongly supported than local exhaustion, but retry timing is needed to establish its contribution.

C1W1S4, C1W1S10, C1W1S16 and C1W1S22 show eight busy errors each in DELETE mode, modest I/O full pressure and a 1.050000 completion ratio. Lock contention is observed; which transactions contend and how much latency they cause are uncertain. Missing WAL activity in DELETE mode is not evidence of a checkpoint failure.

The remaining eight cases complete at baseline with low pressure, no errors and checkpoint progress. WAL growth during concurrent writing is not by itself a fault. These finite windows show healthy load, not a maximum sustainable agent count or a provider latency baseline under other conditions.

Logical-to-physical write ratios span 1.000000 to 5.000000. Values above one can reflect cache effects, coalescing, repeated logical accounting or unmatched measurement scopes; they do not establish physical write amplification. Device read and write totals cannot identify SQLite traffic or copy traffic without matched per-process or file attribution. Throughput alone does not establish device saturation.
